evidence: getCurrentSpeed returns [_currentSpeed], which the inline advanceTime (X3DTimeContext.js:36-72) sets once per frame to the distance between the last and the current translation of the active viewpoint's camera-space matrix times the frame rate, the position starting at the origin. Viewer3d::advance_speed does the same on the active layer's bound viewpoint after the frame rate update; Browser.currentSpeed and getCurrentSpeed () read it through the SAI speed operation. The tests run the viewer on a live clock at 60 Hz: a viewpoint moving 1 m per frame reads 60 m/s from the second frame and (10 + load moves) * 60 at the first; a viewpoint that only turns reads 0 after the first frame; both accessors agree on every frame. A scripted run keeps 0 because the pinned recorder pages replace advanceTime (oracle/x_ite-pin/src/anim.html), so the recording is not an answer key for this behavior; the upstream order is from source inspection.
